findings.claim: A muse turn that exits non-zero reports the exit before the MSP stream is validated, so an unsupported MSP schema_version or a drifted model is hidden behind a generic exit message instead of the D6 diagnostic.

evidence.observation: Get-MuseTurnOutcome returns on ExitCode != 0 (exit 2 / 130 / 143 / step-cap / generic) before the malformed-stream check and before the run.model.configured agreement check.
The malformed-stream refusal and the model-drift refusal run only after the exit-0 gate, so they are unreachable on any non-zero exit.
The ledger still records engine_run.msp_schema_version from the stream regardless of outcome, so the version signal is retained even when the message hides it.

findings.remedy: Check Events.Malformed and the ExpectModel agreement before the exit-code branches, or append the stream diagnosis to the exit message.
findings.trigger: A CLI update changes the MSP envelope and the run also exits non-zero, or a failed turn serves a drifted model.
findings.verification: Run the fake with FAKE_MUSE_SCHEMA_VERSION=2 plus FAKE_MUSE_EXIT=1 and confirm bridge_outcome names the exit rather than unsupported MSP version 2.
